speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your new movement disorder, could you describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they first started? Please also let me know if you have started any new medications recently, as this is a common cause.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mention new movements since starting risperidone; are they sudden, jerky, and uncontrollable, or are they slow and writhing? Have you noticed any stiffness in your muscles or a resting tremor in your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Your symptoms are classic for akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotics like risperidone characterized by an inner sense of restlessness and an urgent need to move. I will adjust your medication regimen to manage this discomfort; please hold off on any further changes until we review the new prescription together.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
